newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GOLF-STRUEVER AND CLAYDON SHARE TOP SPOT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-STRUEVER AND CLAYDON SHARE TOP SPOT.

text.p: Britain's Russell Claydon missed a four-foot birdie putt on the last green on Saturday to allow German Sven Struever to catch him for a share of the lead after three rounds of the Dutch Open.

Claydon's six-under-par 65 hauled him to a 13-under total of 200 but he was left to regret his miss on the 18th when Struever, who started the day three shots ahead of the field, birdied three of the last four holes. That helped the German to a 69 and a share of first place.
The pair were two shots ahead of South African Wayne Westner, who posted a 68 for 202, one better than compatriot Roger Wessels and Sweden's Daniel Chopra.
Chopra strung together six successive birdies from the 12th to come home in 29 for a 65. He single-putted 13 successive greens from the fifth.
"It was disappointing to miss the birdie chance on the last," said Claydon, who has finished second five times but never won on the European Tour.
Struever was relieved to hit back after suffering in the middle of his round. "It feels good to have finished so well and perhaps the bad run taught me a vital lesson for the final round," he said.
